uslaw-usc-t2-s179o:
Section 179o of Title 2 of the United States Code states the duties of the National Film Preservation Board. The board works with the Librarian of Congress on the National Film Registry. The registry names films worth saving for the nation.

The board's first duty is review. It examines nominations of films sent to it for the registry. It consults with the Librarian, under section 179m, on including films in the registry. The same consultation covers preserving those films and other significant ones. Significance is measured three ways: cultural, historical, or aesthetic. A second part opens the door to the public. The board must consider nominations submitted by the general public, not only by experts. Representatives of the film world also feed the list, as the text continues. The section makes film preservation a shared judgment of board, Librarian, and public.
